setup.pitch: For as long as anyone in Briar Glen can remember, the iron lantern in the square has burned without oil. Tonight it is dark. Mara Venn hires the party to recover a stolen ember called the Emberglass before moonrise — but the thief may have taken it because the lantern was never a blessing.
setup.gmSummary: Mara Venn’s family has used the village lantern as a prison for a memory-eating spirit, the Pale Guest. Brother Caldus stole the Emberglass because the old seal is failing. He is at Bellweather Priory trying to bind the spirit properly. The party can restore the old lantern-seal (temporary safety), help Caldus finish a new binding, smash the Emberglass and fight, or bargain a memory for a memory. Required truths have backup routes. Moonrise is the hard clock. This is Episode 1 of The Quiet Seals. Keep the six recommended of twelve pregens. The chosen ending is fact for Episode 2: The Well That Would Not Dry.
setup.campaignFrame: Mayor Cald Wren of Hearthford sent the party to Briar Glen. Mara Venn is the local contact. When this night ends, they return to Hearthford. Mark Wren Helped. If they kept Tamsin or Caldus alive and honest, note it.

quest.objective: Recover the Emberglass and decide how to stop the Pale Guest before moonrise.
quest.stakes: If the seal fails completely, the Pale Guest can reach Briar Glen and feed on the memories of its people.
quest.deadline: Moonrise, roughly four hours after the adventure begins.
successConditions: The Pale Guest remains contained, destroyed, or bound by a new agreement.
The party resolves the fate of the Emberglass.
failureConditions: The Pale Guest escapes the priory without a new binding.
The party abandons the crisis past moonrise.

facts.text: The village lantern and the Emberglass are parts of the same magical seal.
Brother Caldus stole the Emberglass from Briar Glen.
Caldus took the Emberglass to Bellweather Priory.
A memory-devouring spirit called the Pale Guest is bound beneath the priory.

secrets.revealCondition: Speak with Caldus, read his notes, or inspect the ritual chamber.

locations.name: Briar Glen
locations.description: A hill village of forty roofs around a square of packed clay. The iron lantern hangs from a post that has been painted and scraped a dozen times.

locations.name: North Trail
locations.description: Beech and blackthorn, rain-cut ruts, one set of fresh boot prints going north.

locations.name: Old Culvert
locations.description: Shoulder-wide priory drain. Soft candle, scratched warning, crypt at the far end.

locations.name: Bellweather Priory Yard
locations.description: Sixty by fifty feet. Toppled bells, chalked doors, thorned graves, culvert outside the east wall.

locations.name: Ruined Chapel
locations.description: Roofless. Dragged altar, moon-bell plate, hanging handbell, Caldus’s notes.

locations.name: Bell Crypt

locations.description: Forty-foot circle, silver ring, four sigils, Emberglass socket, no second door.

scenes.title: The Dark Lantern
scenes.purpose: Give the quest, establish the deadline, and seed that Mara is withholding information.
scenes.readAloud:
You came up from Hearthford because Mayor Wren asked. The lantern is Briar Glen’s problem, he said. Then he counted to ten and added: if it goes out, the ridge goes with it.

Rain beads on the iron lantern in Briar Glen’s square. The glass is soot-black, the chain still, the flame gone — the first time anyone living has seen it dark. People keep to the porch-eaves. No one stands directly under it.

Mara Venn comes down the steps of the meeting-house with a velvet-lined box held in both hands. The hollow in the lining is the size of a fist. Behind her, a girl with mud to the knees — Tamsin Reed — watches you the way a person watches a door they have already decided to follow.

“It burned for my grandmother, and hers,” Mara says, not quite looking at the lantern. “Brother Caldus took the heart of it. I will pay two hundred gold if you bring the Emberglass back before the moon clears the ridge.”
gmNotes: Pay: 200 gp total, on village survival — even if the Emberglass is not returned (she will not say that yet).
Clock: moonrise in about four hours of play. Name it. Put a token on the table if you want.
Mara’s first story: sacred relic, village luck, Caldus a desperate thief. She will not say ‘seal’ unless pressed (DC 12 Insight/Persuasion — see Checks) or shown evidence.
Tamsin will interrupt if ignored: she saw Caldus take the north trail, and she knows an old culvert. Treat her as an adult and she tells both.
If the party refuses the job, do not end the session. The lantern ticks. A pale mist will reach the square by scene three anyway — use recovery route recover-refuse.
Do not mention the Pale Guest by name. Mara does not use it.

runSteps.title: Name the job and clock
runSteps.text: Mara offers 200 gp if Briar Glen survives and asks for the Emberglass before moonrise. Put the moonrise deadline in front of the table.

runSteps.title: Let the secret show
runSteps.text: If the party presses Mara, use check-mara. Tamsin interrupts if ignored and can identify the north trail plus the old culvert.

runSteps.title: Choose the approach
runSteps.text: Let the party take the north trail, go directly to the priory, or use the culvert if they learned it. Do not force the travel scene.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party leaves Briar Glen for the north trail, priory, or known culvert.

scenes.title: Whispers on the North Trail
scenes.purpose: Provide a flexible travel complication and show the supernatural threat reaching beyond the priory.
scenes.readAloud:
The north trail is a wet cut between blackthorn and beech. Your boots find the ruts of a single walker who did not care who followed.

Three people stand in the road as if they were placed there. A woman in a drover’s coat, a boy with a satchel, an old man still holding a walking stick. They look at one another with the particular fear of people who have lost the last hour of their lives. The boy says, very carefully, “I know I came from somewhere.”

A pale film still hangs in the hollows between the roots, like breath that has not decided to leave.
gmNotes: Cut this whole scene if you are behind clock. The spirit-clue still exists on Caldus later.
They are not undead. They are frightened. Hostile approach scatters them; the clue is not lost — tracks and cold mist still point north.
Check: DC 12 Medicine or Persuasion to calm them (see Checks). Success: they remember pale mist sliding down from the priory ridge, and that it ‘took the names we were using.’
If asked who they are: they can give names after a minute (Dora Fen, Kit, Old Pell). They cannot remember why they were on the trail.
The mist does 0 damage here. It is a warning, not a fight.

runSteps.title: Show the cost of the leak
runSteps.text: Present the three memory-struck travelers and the pale mist pointing back toward the priory ridge.

runSteps.title: Calm or pass them
runSteps.text: Use check-travelers if the party helps. If they continue north, preserve the route and move the spirit clue forward to Caldus.

runSteps.title: Approach the priory
runSteps.text: Let the party choose the broken gate or the culvert if they know it.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party reaches Bellweather Priory or turns into the old culvert.

scenes.title: The Broken Bell Gate
scenes.purpose: Offer combat or bypass and establish that Caldus is preparing, not looting.
scenes.readAloud:
Bellweather Priory sits on the ridge like a broken tooth. Two bronze bells have been dragged into the yard and left on their sides; rainwater ticks inside them.

Fresh white chalk rings the chapel doors — tight, careful circles, not graffiti. Thorn has eaten the grave-row. Something under that thorn shifts when your weight hits the mud, as if four bodies rolled over in their sleep.

The culvert mouth, if Tamsin described it, is a dark slot in the east bank outside the wall. The yard is sixty feet of bad ground.
gmNotes: Wards: DC 12 Arcana/Religion reads them as protective and recent — Caldus’s work, not a cult.
Grave-Things: four, AC 12, 18 HP (Encounters). They rise if anyone moves more than 10 feet into the yard. They do not pursue beyond the wall.
Bypass: culvert if known. Or DC 12 group Stealth along the grave-edge; failure starts the fight 20 feet away.
Fire: if fire damages a Grave-Thing, that one attacks the fire’s source next turn. They are rooted dead, not an army.
Do not run this as a slog. One round of pressure, then remind them of the culvert and the chapel doors.

runSteps.title: Show protective preparation
runSteps.text: Put the fresh chalk wards and toppled bells in view before the Grave-Things rise. check-wards can identify the marks as protective.

runSteps.title: Cross the yard
runSteps.text: Run the guardians only as long as they remain an obstacle. Stealth or the culvert are full solutions, not lesser outcomes.

runSteps.title: Enter the priory
runSteps.text: Once the party reaches the chapel doors or leaves for the culvert, end the yard pressure.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party reaches the chapel or deliberately takes the culvert route.

scenes.title: The Forgotten Culvert
scenes.purpose: Reward investigation and provide an alternate route that bypasses the yard fight.
scenes.readAloud:
The culvert is shoulder-wide, stone, and older than the chapel. Meltwater runs over your boots. Halfway in, a cheap tallow candle is wedged in a crack; the wax is still soft.

Scratched into the lintel, in a neat, angry hand: DO NOT RING THE BELL.

The far end smells of wet bronze and old incense. It opens into the crypt, not the chapel.
gmNotes: Candle less than an hour old — Caldus is still here.
The warning is his. Ringing the crypt bell later feeds the Pale Guest (trap in chapel/crypt).
No fight here. If they make noise, Grave-Things in the yard stir but cannot reach this tunnel.
This route skips the yard combat entirely. That is allowed. Do not punish it.

runSteps.title: Reward the alternate route
runSteps.text: Show the fresh candle and Caldus's DO NOT RING THE BELL warning. Make clear someone has been through recently.

runSteps.title: Preserve the warning
runSteps.text: The scratched message is the clue. Noise may stir the yard guardians, but they cannot enter the culvert.

runSteps.title: Open into the crypt
runSteps.text: Move directly to Caldus once the party reaches the far end.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party reaches the Bell Crypt.

scenes.title: The Open-Sky Chapel
scenes.purpose: Present the puzzle and reveal Caldus's intent.
scenes.readAloud:
The chapel has no roof. Rain falls on pews that have gone to mushroom and black wood. Someone has dragged the altar three feet off its mark. Under it, a bronze plate is set in the floor: four small bells in a row, each stamped with a moon — new, crescent, half, full.

A handbell hangs from a nail by the south stair-well, polished from recent use. Scattered on the wet stone: pages in Caldus’s hand, weighted with a broken roof-slate. The first line you can read without touching anything is: ‘The village flame was never a blessing. It was a door we kept shut.’
gmNotes: Puzzle: press darkest to brightest — new, crescent, half, full. Crypt stair opens. Wrong order: a whisper-pulse, then reset. No damage the first time; second time 1d4 psychic and reset.
Fail forward: ringing the hanging handbell opens the stair AND triggers trap-memory-bell (DC 13 Wisdom; 2d6 psychic; forget the last minute fictionally — players keep all discovered clues).
Caldus’s notes here deliver clue-caldus-binding even if they never meet him politely.
He is not in this room. He is below.

runSteps.title: Put the puzzle and notes together
runSteps.text: Show the four moon bells, the hanging handbell, and Caldus's notes before asking what the party does.

runSteps.title: Open the stair
runSteps.text: The clean solution is new → crescent → half → full. Wrong attempts reset; the hanging bell remains the fail-forward route with its listed psychic cost.

runSteps.title: Carry the truth downstairs
runSteps.text: Make sure Caldus's notes reveal that the village flame was a seal before the party descends.

scenes.advanceWhen: The crypt stair is open and the party descends with Caldus's intent available.

scenes.title: The Bell Crypt
scenes.purpose: Deliver the major revelation and let the party meet Caldus before the finale.
scenes.readAloud:
The crypt is a low stone room with niches like empty mouths. A cracked bronze bell hangs dead-center, its clapper wrapped in torn vestments. Cloth, not rust, is what keeps it quiet.

Brother Caldus stands on the far side of it. He looks like a man who has not slept in three days. In his left hand is a fist-sized coal of red-gold glass — warm light leaking between his fingers. His right hand is up, empty, not a weapon.

“If you came to hang a thief,” he says, very carefully, “wait until I have finished the sentence. The lantern in your square is a lock. I stole the key because the lock is breaking.”
gmNotes: He does not attack first. If they talk, he tells the whole truth: Emberglass + lantern = failing seal; Pale Guest feeds on memory; he wants a new binding in the chamber below.
If they attack: enc-caldus-if-hostile. AC 13, 36 HP. He retreats toward the ritual stair, shouts the truth every round, surrenders at 8 HP. Journal still delivers required clues if he drops.
If they agree to help: he becomes an ally, hands off the Emberglass or keeps it for the ritual (their call), and leads them down.
Do not make them fight a paladin-boss here. This is the twist scene. The fight is below.

runSteps.title: Give Caldus one sentence
runSteps.text: He does not attack first. Let him state that the lantern is a failing lock before the party decides whether to hear more.

runSteps.title: Resolve trust or hostility
runSteps.text: If they talk, he explains the Pale Guest and new binding. If attacked, use the defensive encounter while his warnings or journal preserve the same revelation.

runSteps.title: Go to the ritual chamber
runSteps.text: Once the party understands the real stakes—or has the journal after a fight—move to the chamber below.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party descends to the ritual chamber with the seal truth available through Caldus or his journal.

scenes.title: The Pale Guest
scenes.purpose: Resolve the quest through combat, ritual, negotiation, or a combination.
scenes.readAloud:
The chamber is a forty-foot circle of black stone. A silver ring in the floor is already hairline-cracked. Four sigils mark the cardinal points. In the center, a socket waits for the Emberglass — or shows the empty place where it should sit.

The ring splits with a sound like ice going on a lake. A tall figure unfolds from the far dark: no face, too many mouths, each whispering in a voice someone in the party almost knows. A mother. A dead friend. A child you have not met yet.

“You kept me in a lamp,” the mouths say together, almost kindly. “Choose better.”
gmNotes: Roll initiative after the read-aloud. Pale Guest: AC 14, 88 HP, fly 30 hover. See Encounters for attacks, Whispering Theft, Unstable Binding.

Three legal victories: (1) 0 HP — destroy it. (2) 3 ritual successes before 3 failures — bind it (check-ritual DC 13; Caldus auto-success end of round 2 if allied and up). (3) 3 bargain successes before 2 failures — new pact (check-bargain DC 15; cost = one meaningful memory per willing bargainer). Record the memories.
Smash Emberglass (action, holding it): Guest loses nonmagical weapon resistance; binding becomes impossible.
It does not leave this room while the Emberglass exists. No fleeing. If the party runs upstairs, moonrise still comes — recovery, not a chase map.
Keep rounds short. Narrate one whisper per round. Do not erase character sheets; memory-loss is story, except the listed psychic damage.

Fourth legal victory — Restore the Old Flame: requires the intact Emberglass. Get three successes before two failures. During initiative, one character may spend their action on one attempt; the Pale Guest otherwise acts normally.

Old Flame checks: DC 13 Arcana, Religion, Athletics, or Persuasion when the approach fits. A different proficient skill is DC 14 with a concrete fictional approach. No character makes more than one attempt per round.

Old Flame pressure: on a failed attempt, the acting character takes 1d6 psychic damage and the Pale Guest immediately uses Whispering Theft against that character if able. If Caldus is allied and conscious, once during this challenge he may spend his action to grant advantage on one attempt.

Old Flame result: at three successes, the Guest is pulled back into the old lantern-seal and initiative ends. At two failures, this option closes for the scene but binding, bargaining, and combat remain available. Caldus warns the repaired seal will fail within roughly one season.

runSteps.title: Put every legal victory on the table
runSteps.text: The party can destroy the Guest, complete the replacement binding, bargain with it, or restore the old flame while the Emberglass remains intact.

runSteps.title: Run pressure, not hidden rules
runSteps.text: Use initiative, the sigil flare, and the listed ritual/bargain/Old Flame procedures. Tell players when an action advances one of those tracks.

runSteps.title: Honor the Emberglass choice
runSteps.text: If it is smashed, remove nonmagical resistance and close binding/Old Flame as written. Do not invent another penalty.

runSteps.title: End when one resolution succeeds
runSteps.text: Stop initiative immediately when a legal resolution completes and carry that exact state into What Burns After.

scenes.advanceWhen: The Pale Guest is destroyed, newly bound, bargained with, or returned to the old lantern-seal.

scenes.title: What Burns After
scenes.purpose: Close the adventure and make the party's choice matter.
scenes.readAloud:
Dawn at Briar Glen is ordinary weather and an extraordinary quiet. People come out to look at the iron lantern as if it might speak.

Mara is already in the square. She does not ask whether you are heroes. She asks what you did with the thing that used to burn there — and whether the village still has a secret, a prison, a grave, or a debt.

A drover on the north road, if anyone is still listening, says the well at Saltmere has gone wrong. Iron in the water. Names that will not stick. That is tomorrow’s problem. Tonight, end on the lantern.
gmNotes: Restore old flame: lantern lights again. Caldus, if alive, says it will fail within a season. Mara pays. The secret can stay buried or not — party’s word. Episode 2: Saltmere has heard the lantern ‘held.’ They want the same trick for their well.
New binding: lantern stays dark, a memorial. Priory holds. Mara pays. Caldus may stay as keeper. Episode 2: Saltmere wants Caldus or the party, not the old lantern-method.
Destroyed: no cage. Some villagers hate the party for killing the luck. Mara still pays if they lived. Episode 2: Saltmere is terrified you will smash their well-charm too.
Bargain: Guest gone for now. Write the owed memories. Mara pays, shaken. Episode 2: something in Saltmere already knows the names you sold.
200 gp from Mara if the glen survives. Moonstones in the crypt if they search after.
Do not play Episode 2 tonight unless you have it. Write the ending on the campaign card and stop. Same six characters next session.

runSteps.title: Name what happened
runSteps.text: Use the ending that actually occurred: old flame, new binding, destruction, or bargain. State the immediate village consequence.

runSteps.title: Pay and record
runSteps.text: Mara pays 200 gp if Briar Glen survives. Record the campaign fact, any owed memories, and whether Caldus/Tamsin remain trusted contacts.

runSteps.title: Close on the next consequence
runSteps.text: Give the Saltmere hook appropriate to the ending, then stop the session rather than beginning another episode inside this one.

scenes.advanceWhen: The ending, payment, and campaign fact are recorded.

clues.revelation: Caldus took the Emberglass toward Bellweather Priory.
sources: Tamsin saw him take the north trail
fresh tracks from the lantern square lead north

clues.revelation: Mara is withholding the true purpose of the Emberglass.
Something from the priory can steal recent memories.
Caldus has been placing protections around the priory rather than desecrating it.
Ringing the cracked bell strengthens the Pale Guest's influence.
Caldus is attempting to create a replacement binding.
The Emberglass is part of a seal containing the Pale Guest.
Caldus stole the Emberglass to replace the failing seal, not to profit from it.
sources: completed portions of the new binding

encounters.name: Memory-Struck Travelers
encounters.summary: Three travelers are confused and frightened. Calming them reveals that a pale mist from the priory stole recent memories.
encounters.resolution: No combat required. A hostile approach may scatter them and lose this optional clue.
encounters.talkOut: Persuasion or Medicine DC 12: they stay and describe the mist. Intimidation scatters them.
encounters.special: Not a fight unless the party attacks. They scatter if intimidated.
encounters.objective: Learn what the pale mist did without turning frightened victims into an unnecessary fight.

encounters.name: Thornbound Grave-Things
encounters.summary: Four vine-wrapped dead guardians rise from the graves. They do not pursue beyond the priory yard.
encounters.resolution: Fight them, distract them with fire/noise, or bypass them through the culvert.
encounters.bypass: Culvert or fire/noise. They do not speak.
encounters.special: Ambush if the party walks the grave-row without checking. Fight to the death. They do not speak and do not chase past the broken gate.
encounters.objective: Cross the priory yard or neutralize the rooted guardians long enough to reach shelter.

encounters.name: Brother Caldus
encounters.summary: Caldus wants to talk. If attacked, he fights defensively and retreats toward the ritual chamber.
encounters.resolution: The scene should still deliver the seal revelation through his shouted warnings, notes, or ritual evidence.
encounters.talkOut: He wants to talk. Persuasion DC 13 to help the new binding; Insight DC 12 to see he is telling the truth.
encounters.special: Wants to talk first. Fights defensively and retreats to the ritual chamber if attacked. Does not fight to the death.
encounters.objective: Keep the seal revelation available while deciding whether Caldus becomes an ally, prisoner, or obstacle.

encounters.name: The Pale Guest
encounters.summary: A memory-eating spirit attacks while the binding fails. Each round should create pressure through whispers, lost recollections, or unstable sigils.
encounters.resolution: Defeat it, complete the replacement binding, destroy the Emberglass and fight it fully, or negotiate a costly new bargain.
encounters.talkOut: Bargain: a memory for a memory. It does not need to be a boss fight.
encounters.special: Appears after the read-aloud; roll initiative. Will negotiate (see talk-out). Does not leave this chamber while the Emberglass exists.
encounters.objective: Stop the Pale Guest before moonrise through destruction, binding, bargain, or restoration of the old seal.

puzzles.name: Four Moons Lock
puzzles.prompt: Four engraved bells are marked new moon, crescent, half, and full.
puzzles.solution: Press them from darkest to brightest: new, crescent, half, full.
puzzles.failForward: A wrong sequence emits a whispering pulse and then resets. The crypt can also be opened by ringing the handbell, at a cost.

traps.name: Memory Bell
traps.effect: Each nearby creature makes a Wisdom saving throw DC 13. Failure: lose a trivial recent memory and hear the Pale Guest. Success: hear the whisper, keep the memory. Either way the crypt stair is obvious — fail-forward.
traps.purpose: Failure advances the adventure but increases supernatural pressure.

items.name: Emberglass
items.description: A fist-sized coal of translucent red-gold glass that remains warm without flame.

events.name: Moonrise
events.effect: The failing seal breaks completely and the Pale Guest can escape if not contained.

policies: Preserve established facts, not a predetermined route.
Never erase a successful player deduction.
Move a required clue only to a plausible authored backup source.
Record state changes when recovery changes where information is found.

routes.trigger: The party refuses Mara's quest or does not trust her.
routes.response: Tamsin approaches them privately and reveals she followed Caldus toward Bellweather Priory. The village lantern then emits a brief pulse of pale mist, making the danger immediate.

routes.trigger: Mara is killed, missing, or otherwise unavailable before giving the destination.
routes.response: Tamsin provides the destination. Fresh northbound tracks from the lantern square independently confirm it.

routes.trigger: The party bypasses the chapel and reaches Caldus through the culvert.
routes.response: Do not force them back. Caldus directly explains the replacement binding and the Emberglass's purpose.
stateChanges: Make the two required revelations available in scene-crypt.

routes.trigger: The party attacks Caldus before hearing him out.
routes.response: Caldus shouts that breaking the Emberglass will free the thing below. His dropped journal and the visible ritual provide the same core revelations if he cannot continue speaking.
stateChanges: Preserve access to clue-real-seal and clue-caldus-plan.

routes.trigger: The party destroys the Emberglass before the new binding is complete.
routes.response: Accept the choice. The Pale Guest becomes fully manifest and vulnerable. The objective changes from sealing it to defeating it or bargaining with it.

routes.trigger: The party leaves the priory after learning the truth.
routes.response: The world advances. Pale mist reaches Briar Glen as moonrise approaches. The party may confront Mara, rally villagers, or return by either known route, but the seal continues to fail.
stateChanges: Return current scene to Briar Glen without removing discovered clues.

routes.trigger: The party talks to no one: they refuse Mara, ignore Tamsin, sneak the priory, and never hear Caldus.
routes.response: Do not stop the game. Tracks go north. Chapel notes, crypt inscriptions, and the unfinished binding still deliver every required fact. The Pale Guest still manifests. Caldus, if found dead or bypassed, is optional.
stateChanges: Discover all required clues from physical sources.

cutOrder: If 30+ minutes behind, cut Whispers on the North Trail entirely; Caldus and the ritual evidence still deliver the spirit truth.
If 20+ minutes behind at the priory, let the culvert route be immediately available if Tamsin described it and skip the yard guardians.
If 15+ minutes behind after the chapel, move directly from the Caldus revelation into the ritual chamber after one clear exchange.

endings.name: Restore the Old Flame
endings.condition: The party returns the Emberglass to the old binding.
endings.result: Briar Glen is safe for now. Anyone who studied the priory (Caldus if alive, otherwise his notes) can warn that the old seal will fail again.

endings.name: A Stronger Bell
endings.condition: The party completes the replacement binding in the chamber. Caldus is not required.
endings.result: The Pale Guest is bound beneath the priory. The village lantern becomes a memorial. If Caldus lived, he may stay as keeper; if not, the binding still holds.

endings.name: No More Cages
endings.condition: The party destroys the Emberglass and defeats the Pale Guest.
endings.result: The old bargain ends permanently. Briar Glen must live without the protection or secrecy of the lantern.

endings.name: A Memory for a Memory
endings.condition: The party negotiates a new bargain with the Pale Guest.
endings.result: The spirit withdraws, but the agreed cost becomes part of the campaign's history.

checks.label: Press Mara for the truth
checks.success: Mara admits the Emberglass is part of a protective seal and identifies Bellweather Priory.
checks.failure: She still names the priory but withholds the seal's purpose; Tamsin can reveal the alternate route.

checks.label: Calm the memory-struck travelers
checks.success: They remember pale mist drifting from the priory and reveal clue-spirit-nature.
checks.failure: They scatter, but tracks and cold mist still point toward the priory; no required clue is lost.

checks.label: Read the chalk wards
checks.success: The marks are protective and recently renewed by Caldus.
checks.failure: The marks remain obviously fresh; Caldus or his notes can reveal their purpose later.

checks.label: Advance the replacement binding
checks.failure: No progress; the acting character takes 1d6 psychic damage from the Guest's whispers.

checks.label: Negotiate with the Pale Guest
checks.success: Gain 1 bargain success; 3 before 2 failures produces a binding bargain.
checks.failure: Gain 1 bargain failure and the Guest immediately uses Whispering Theft against the speaker.

encounters.objective: Calm the travelers long enough to learn what happened on the road.
encounters.start: Three frightened travelers stumble from the north trail unable to agree on where they came from or what they lost.
encounters.bypass: The party may ignore them and continue north; the spirit clue remains available from Caldus later.
encounters.end: Use check-travelers. On success they describe pale mist from the priory; on failure they scatter, but tracks and cold mist still point north.

encounters.objective: Cross the yard or neutralize the guardians.
encounters.start: Four Thornbound Grave-Things rise when a creature moves more than 10 feet into the yard.
encounters.bypass: Characters who know the culvert can skip this encounter. A DC 12 Dexterity (Stealth) group check also crosses the grave edge without waking them; on failure combat starts with the Grave-Things 20 feet away.

creatures.name: Thornbound Grave-Thing
creatures.attack: Thorn Claw. Melee +4 to hit, reach 5 ft.; 1d6+2 slashing.
creatures.trait: Rooted Dead. Difficult terrain caused by plants does not slow it. It never pursues beyond the priory yard.
creatures.tactics: Attack the nearest intruder. If fire damages one, that creature attacks the source of the fire on its next turn.

encounters.end: Combat ends when all guardians are destroyed or no conscious party member remains in the yard. Fleeing into the chapel ends pursuit.

encounters.objective: Keep the revelation available even if talks collapse.
encounters.start: Caldus begins 25 feet away and does not attack first.

creatures.name: Brother Caldus
creatures.attack: Ash Staff. Melee +4 to hit; 1d6+2 bludgeoning plus 1d4 fire.
creatures.ranged: Ember Bolt. Ranged spell attack +5, range 60 ft.; 2d8 fire.
creatures.reaction: Warding Spark (1/round). Add +2 AC against one attack that would hit him.
creatures.tactics: Disengages toward the ritual chamber when below 18 HP. He calls out the truth about the seal every round and surrenders rather than fight to the death.

encounters.end: At 8 HP or fewer Caldus yields if given the chance. If reduced to 0 HP, his journal beside the Emberglass reveals clue-real-seal and clue-caldus-plan.

encounters.objective: Survive while choosing destruction, binding, or bargain.
encounters.start: The Guest appears at the far side of the 40-foot ritual chamber. Roll initiative immediately after the read-aloud.

creatures.name: The Pale Guest
creatures.resistances: necrotic; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
creatures.attack: Memory Rend. Melee +6 to hit, reach 10 ft.; 2d8+3 psychic.
creatures.action: Whispering Theft. One creature within 60 ft. makes a DC 13 Wisdom save; on failure it takes 3d6 psychic damage and has disadvantage on its next attack roll or ability check. Half damage and no disadvantage on success.
creatures.trait: Unstable Binding. At initiative count 20, one unoccupied sigil flares. A creature adjacent to it may use its reaction to make DC 12 Intelligence (Arcana or Religion); success suppresses the flare, failure or no attempt deals 1d6 psychic damage to every creature within 10 ft. of that sigil.
creatures.tactics: Targets whoever most recently advanced the ritual or bargain. It does not leave the chamber while the Emberglass remains intact. Prepared table: start at 66 HP. Bell rung: 15 temp HP. Zero clues: Whispering Theft on everyone before initiative.

encounters.ritual: The replacement binding needs 3 ritual successes before 3 ritual failures. One character adjacent to a sigil can use an action for check-ritual. Caldus contributes one automatic success at the end of round 2 if conscious and allied. At 3 successes, the Guest is bound and combat ends.
encounters.destroy: A creature holding the Emberglass may use an action to smash it against the central stone. The Guest loses its nonmagical weapon resistance and cannot be bound afterward.
encounters.bargain: A character can use an action for check-bargain. Three bargain successes before two failures ends hostilities, but the party must offer one meaningful memory from each willing bargainer; record the memories as story consequences.
encounters.end: 0 HP destroys the Guest; 3 ritual successes bind it; 3 bargain successes create a new pact.

hazards.trigger: A character rings the hanging handbell.
hazards.failure: Take 2d6 psychic damage and forget the last minute until finishing a short rest; the player still retains all discovered clues and game information.
hazards.success: Half damage and no memory loss.
hazards.failForward: The crypt stair opens either way.

rewards.reward: Mara pays the promised 200 gp total even if the Emberglass is not returned.

rewards.when: The party searches the crypt after resolving the finale.
rewards.reward: A hidden votive box contains 80 gp in old silver and two 50 gp moonstones.

rewards.when: The party completes the new binding without destroying the Emberglass.
rewards.reward: Each surviving character gains Ember's Resolve: once before the next long rest, add 1d4 to a failed Wisdom saving throw, then the blessing ends.

rewards.when: Prepared: Mara alive and not publicly denounced.
rewards.reward: After the crowd leaves, she presses a 50 gp purse into someone's hand. 'For not making a speech.'

rewards.when: Prepared: they spoke with Tamsin before leaving the square.
rewards.reward: She slips them a healer's kit and a loaf. 'If you die on that road I have to look at your horse.'

informationContract.rule: No required fact depends on one NPC being alive, friendly, or present.

requiredFacts.ifTheySkip: Tamsin, northbound tracks, or the mist itself.
Chapel notes or the ritual chamber even if Caldus is dead.
Mara if pressed, crypt inscriptions, Caldus or his journal.
Journal and the unfinished binding. His speech is one path, not the path.

informationContract.finaleWithoutNpc: The Pale Guest scene does not require Caldus. He is an extra ritual success if allied and conscious. Binding, destruction, and bargain all work without him.

pathPressure.principle: The ending is never locked. A table that does the work gets paid and the last fight is shorter. A table that murders, rings the bell, or skips every clue still finishes — they spend more hit points and leave gold on the table.
notDeviation: The culvert is an authored route, not a rush.
Sneaking or bargaining past the grave-things is smart play, not deviation.
Helping Caldus, restoring the old seal, destroying the Guest, or bargaining are all valid endings.
